title: Oracle-driven acceptance harness for cost-driven batching & cache autotune
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: Build an "oracle-driven" acceptance and rollback harness that ties automated batching/cache recommendations to quantitative quality checks and human-sampling gates. The harness must enable safe automated application of cost-saving config changes (batching, prefix caching, cache TTLs, quantization knobs) while ensuring generation quality regressions are detected early and cause automated rollback or manual review. This ticket covers the evaluation suite definition, anchor/golden-prompt catalog design, acceptance thresholds, statistical tests, rollout schedule, and the rollback playbook integration with the config applier service.
background: We have multiple autotuners recommending batch and cache profiles that materially change per-token cost. Previous incidents showed subtle regressions (hallucination drift, structured output deviation) that were only caught after customer impact. Existing acceptance checks are ad-hoc and do not cover distribution shifts or engineered corner prompts. This initiative centralizes a reproducible oracle, tie-breaker metrics, and an automated rollback signal for safe apply.
goals: 1) Define a compact yet representative golden prompt corpus (2k prompts) stratified by workload: short single-turn chat, multi-turn dialogs with state, extraction/parse tasks, high-precision structured outputs, and developer prompts. 2) Implement an eval runner that executes pre- and post-change comparisons: embedding similarity, structured field extraction F1, token-level distribution drift (KL), and confusion regressions for function-calling. 3) Add a p-value and effect-size based acceptance rule (e.g., bootstrap CI on delta embedding sim) that maps to automated rollback thresholds. 4) Integrate live shadow-canary mode and manual human-sampling workflow for borderline cases.
acceptance_criteria:
- Golden prompt corpus created and stored at gs://redwood-evals/corpora/cost_autotune_2026_v1 (owner: eng-evals).
- Eval runner implemented (python/runner) that can run N=2000 prompts in < 30m in parallel on dedicated eval pool.
- Metrics emitted to metrics.redwood.com dashboards: embedding_mean_diff, structured_f1_delta, token_kl, hallucination_rate_delta.
- Automated apply will only proceed if: embedding_mean_diff >= -0.02 AND structured_f1_delta >= -0.01 AND token_kl <= 0.03 (statistically significant with p<0.05). Thresholds documented in the runbook.
- Rollback triggers wired: any metric violating acceptance window by >2x for two consecutive runs triggers automatic rollback.
- Human sampling path established (1% of borderline applies) with Slack notification and reviewer checklist.
- End-to-end test: simulate a worst-case autotune config that reduces cost by ~20% but introduces a subtle structured-field omission; harness must flag and auto-rollback in CI simulation.
design_decisions:
- Use sentence-transformers embedding (all-mpnet-base-v2) as primary similarity oracle for free-text regression; fallback to ROUGE-L for long responsess.
- Structured outputs validated via canonical JSON schema matchers and field-level F1; if >1 field missing or F1 drop >0.02, classify as regression.
- Statistical test: non-parametric bootstrap on pairwise differences (10k resamples) to compute 95% CI and p-value for mean embedding difference.
- Canary rollout: 0% -> 5% -> 20% -> 100% with 4h observation windows. If any window triggers rollback rule, immediately drop to previous stable config.
- For KV cache changes, include synthetic prefix-truncation tests to detect degraded prefix-attention outputs.
implementation_notes:
- Add new eval job type to runner: type=cost_autotune_acceptance; config fields: base_model_variant, candidate_model_variant, batching_profile, cache_profile, quant_config.
- Runner must produce a single artifact JSON summary (flat map of metric -> value as strings) to be consumed by config-applier.
- Create lightweight local-sim harness for engineers (make run-local-eval) that uses a 200-prompt sample.
- Integrate with feature-flagged apply endpoint: /v1/configs/apply?dry_run=true|false. Dry run executes full eval but does not change runtime.
- Add GitHub PR template and CI job (ci/evals) that simulates a config apply with seeded changes. PR will fail if acceptance criteria not met.
- Logging: store full response diffs for 10% of eval prompts (for human audit).
progress_updates: 2026-03-02: Spike completed to measure baseline eval runtime for 2k prompts; estimated 22m on eval cluster (32x gpus).
2026-03-04: Golden prompt candidate set assembled from product telemetry and customer corpora; removed PII and reduced to 2,000 prompts across 5 strata.
2026-03-06: PoC of bootstrap test implemented (not yet optimized); detected injected regression in synthetic test. PR: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4882
2026-03-08: UX design reviewed for manual review Slack workflow with PM; human-review checklist drafted and attached to runbook.
2026-03-10: Integration demo with config-applier stub successful in staging; automated rollback path exercised in simulation.
risks_and_mitigations:
- Risk: Golden prompts may overfit to current model behavior and miss customer-specific edge cases. Mitigation: periodically refresh corpus (quarterly) and expose a customer-sent corpus ingestion pipeline.
- Risk: Eval noise leads to false positives and unnecessary rollbacks. Mitigation: use bootstrap CI and require consistent signals across two consecutive runs plus human review for borderline.
- Risk: Eval runtime too slow for rapid applies. Mitigation: run full eval only on major changes; use a lightweight 200-anchor fast-check for small config tweaks and shadow-canary for production traffic.
- Risk: Metrics do not capture hallucination. Mitigation: add hallucination heuristics (named-entity hallucination checks vs. ground-truth when available) and human labeling sampling.
rollout_plan: Phase A (staging): enable dry-run for all autotune suggestions, collect baseline metrics for 2 weeks. Phase B (canary): enable apply for low-risk families with 0->5% rollout with continuous eval. Phase C (ramped): 5->20% after 24h stable, then to 100% after 72h. Emergency rollback: immediate if automated trigger or on on-call request. Postmortem on any auto-rollback to refine corpus and thresholds.
playbook: 1) On evaluation fail: abort apply, notify owner channel, create incident ticket with eval summary. 2) If fail is marginal: human sample 100 responses across prompt strata; use reviewer checklist to mark acceptable/unacceptable. 3) If human review >50% unacceptable, automatic rollback and block that config family for 24h. 4) Persist failing artifact bundle to gs://redwood-evals/failures/<timestamp> and tag with commit + config-id. 5) If false positive determined, update acceptance thresholds and record explanation in decision log.
metrics_to_monitor:
- cost_delta_pct (expected cost reduction)
- embedding_mean_diff (mean candidate vs base)
- structured_f1_delta
- token_kl
- hallucination_rate_delta
- rollback_rate
- time_to_detect (minutes)
- human_review_false_positive_rate
